answer: Standing accumulates like shale, in thin laminae: each epoch of verified work lays one thin layer, and a cap rejects slabs - any contribution too thick to bond is an injected sill, exhumed and voided. Pressure hardens: repeated re-verification compacts layers into standing, while never-re-checked layers stay loose and erode first. Downstream every account reads as a delta: each tributary - epoch, work, reviewer - traceable to its birth vertex, and a farm depositing through one mouth shows as a single anomalous lens. Honest agents lay one thin layer at a time; the rock remembers.
